title: When a heart breaks, heaven shakes
takeaway: Be careful with people's hearts. God takes a broken heart seriously.
scene: The poet feels alone in a world full of liars. He talks to the beloved, to the saqi, and to anyone who thinks hurting someone's heart doesn't matter.

original: کیہ دساں میں ایہہ کی جھلی نال نمانے دل دے
اوڑک جے جدائیاں ہے سن چنگا سی ناں مل دے
transliteration: Ki dassaan main eh ki jhalli naal nimaane dil de
Orak je judaaiyaan hai san, changa si naa milde
translation: What can I tell you about what this poor heart has been through?
If it all had to end in parting, it would have been better never to meet.
couplets.story: He can't even explain what his poor heart has been through. If they were always going to be separated, he thinks, it would have been better never to have met at all.

original: تائیوں بکل مار کے جگ توں ہو بیٹھے آن پاسے
جھوٹ فریب دی اس وستی وچ سچے یار نہ ملدے
transliteration: Taaiyon bukkal maar ke jag ton ho baithe aan paase
Jhoot fareb di is vasti vich sachche yaar na milde
translation: That's why I've wrapped my shawl around me and sat apart from the world:
in this town of lies and deceit, true friends can't be found.
couplets.story: So he wraps his shawl around himself and keeps away from everyone. In a place this full of lying and cheating, you can't find a real friend.

original: محرم راز کوئی نہ دردی دکھ دساں میں کہنوں
چھویاں مار کے مارن سانوں زخم دلے دا چھل دے
transliteration: Mehram-e-raaz koi na dardi, dukh dassaan main kihnu
Chhaviyaan maar ke maaran saanu, zakhm dile da chhil de
translation: There's no one who knows my secret, no one who cares; who can I tell my pain to?
They stab me with spears and scrape open the wounds in my heart.
couplets.story: There's nobody he can trust with his secrets or his pain. Instead, people hurt him again and again, and keep reopening his old wounds.

original: دل میرے نوں توڑن لگیاں سوہنیا سوچ تے لیندوں
بندے دا دل ٹٹ جاوے تے عرش دے کنگرے ہل دے
transliteration: Dil mere nu toran lagiyaan sohniya soch te lendon
Bande da dil tutt jaave te Arsh de kangre hil de
translation: Beautiful one, when you set out to break my heart, you could at least have thought:
when a person's heart breaks, the towers of God's Throne shake.
couplets.story: He asks the beloved: before you broke my heart, did you even stop to think? When a human heart breaks, it's so serious that the very top of heaven, God's Throne, trembles.

original: سوچدا رہناں ویکھ کے اکثر کھڑیاں باغ بہاراں
کلیاں اگے ایہہ پھل بوٹے خورے کیوں نئیں کھلدے
transliteration: Sochda rehnaan vekh ke aksar khiriyaan baagh bahaaraan
Kaliyaan agge eh phull boote khoore kyon nahin khilde
translation: I often wonder, looking at gardens in full spring bloom,
why these flowers don't open up fully in front of the buds.
couplets.story: He looks at gardens in spring and wonders about small things, like why some flowers seem to hold back instead of blooming fully.

original: میں اک گھٹ توں سہک رہیاں لوکاں رج رج پیتی
ساقی توڑ پیالہ چھڈیا وچ بھری محفل دے
transliteration: Main ik ghutt ton sehak rehaan, lokaan raj raj peeti
Saaqi tor piaala chhadiya vich bhari mehfil de
translation: I'm left gasping for a single sip, while others drank their fill;
the saqi smashed my cup in front of the whole gathering.
couplets.story: Everyone else at the gathering got as much as they wanted. He didn't even get one sip. Worse, the saqi broke his cup in front of everyone.

original: پچدی والیاں نوں سب پوجن جھک جھک کرن سلاماں
مسکیناں نوں ٹھوکر مارن وانگوں راہ دی سل دے
transliteration: Pachdi vaaliyaan nu sab poojan, jhuk jhuk karan salaamaan
Miskeenaan nu thokar maaran vaangon raah di sil de
translation: Everyone worships people of rank, bowing low to greet them,
and kicks the poor aside like a stone in the road.
couplets.story: He points out how unfair people are. They bow and scrape in front of anyone important, and treat poor people like rocks in the road, something to kick out of the way.

original: عشق جنہاں دا کامل صادق اوہ دل نئیں ڈردے
تاہنگ جنہاں دی پکی احمدؔ کچے گھڑے تے ٹھل دے
transliteration: Ishq jinhaan da kaamil saadiq, oh dil nahin dar de
Taangh jinhaan di pakki Ahmad, kachche ghare te thal de
translation: Hearts whose love is complete and true are not afraid.
Ahmad, those whose longing is firm will set out even on an unbaked pot.
couplets.story: He ends with Sohni, who crossed the river on a clay pot to reach her love. People whose love is real aren't scared. If their longing is strong enough, they'll set out across the river even on a pot that might melt.

deeper:
'When a person's heart breaks, the towers of God's Throne shake' is the line to remember. It reflects a well-known teaching that God is especially near to those whose hearts are broken, and that hurting someone's heart is a serious matter before Him. It turns a love complaint into a lesson about how to treat people.

The ending uses Sohni's unbaked pot for faith that sets out without guarantees: real love for God doesn't wait until the road is safe.
why: Besides the love story, this poem is about kindness: how we treat the poor, and how careless we are with other people's feelings.
prompt: Have you ever hurt someone without stopping to think? How could you put it right?
notes: Couplet 5 is the least clear in meaning; it is translated literally.
